abstract: A caller claims to be from the bank's risk/fraud team about an unusual or duplicated transaction and pushes the customer to 'verify' by sharing personal details, a one-time code, or moving money to a 'safe account'.
safe_verification_channel: the number printed on the back of the bank card / the bank's official app
red_flags: request to move money to a safe account

abstract: A caller posing as police/CBI/customs says a parcel or SIM linked to the victim's ID was found with illegal items; the victim is kept on a prolonged video 'investigation', isolated, and pressured to transfer funds to a 'verification account' to prove innocence.
safe_verification_channel: hang up and call the local police non-emergency number directly; real agencies never arrest over a video call

abstract: A friendly contact (wrong-number or dating app) builds rapport over time, then introduces a 'can't-miss' crypto/stock platform, shows small withdrawable profits to build trust, and escalates deposits until withdrawals are blocked.
safe_verification_channel: independent research; a licensed broker verified on the regulator's official register

abstract: A caller claims to be from a well-known tech/antivirus company about a virus or an expiring subscription, directs the victim to install remote-access software, then fakes a refund 'overpayment' to extract money.
safe_verification_channel: the company's official website/app; banks and tech firms never need remote access to your device
red_flags: asks to log into banking while connected
